title: Vendoring: update.sh --add; dagre + graphlib + xterm + addon-fit
what:
vendor/update.sh gains `--add <pkg> <ver>`. It trusts the registry's dist.integrity once and appends the pin to VERSIONS, as --bump does for packages that are already pinned (update.sh:62). Pins and takes:
- @dagrejs/dagre 3.1.1 dist/dagre.esm.js -> vendor/dagre.js ('@dagrejs/graphlib' rewritten to './graphlib.js')
- @dagrejs/graphlib 4.0.5 ESM -> vendor/graphlib.js
- @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 lib/xterm.mjs -> vendor/xterm.js and css/xterm.css -> vendor/xterm.css
- @xterm/addon-fit 0.11.0 lib/addon-fit.mjs -> vendor/addon-fit.js ('@xterm/xterm' rewritten to './xterm.js' if present)
- LICENSE-dagre, LICENSE-graphlib, LICENSE-xterm, LICENSE-xterm-addon-fit
Final checks: no bare import (existing), and a new check for `eval(` or `new Function`, because the CSP has no unsafe-eval.
Never vendor the webgl, canvas (5.x only), clipboard (OSC 52) or web-links addons.
Add vendor/README.md.
Stop and report:
- if dagre's ESM needs more than graphlib (fallback: a hand-made layered layout)
- if xterm.mjs fails a check (the terminal plan then needs your call)
tests:
- `sh vendor/update.sh --check` verifies tarball sha512 against VERSIONS, and a second run is byte-identical.
- vendor.test.mjs lays out a 3-node graph with vendor/dagre.js under node.
- A static scan asserts that xterm.js exports Terminal and has no bare import, no eval and no new Function.
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48105 (after S0P-b): in the browser pane console, `const {Terminal} = await import('/vendor/xterm.js')` opens a Terminal into a detached div with no CSP violation logged.
risk: Needs registry.npmjs.org, which update.sh's design already allows. The bare-import regex may false-positive on strings inside minified code, so inspect once by hand.
